stories.title: Shorenstein Adds 300K-SF Dallas Office Tower to DFW Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Shorenstein Investment Advisers acquired Sherry Lane Place, a 300,000-square-foot Class AA office tower in the Preston Center submarket of Dallas, Texas. The acquisition marks Shorenstein’s fourth acquisition in Dallas over the past two years. Sherry Lane Place is a 20-story, Class AA office tower located in Dallas’ premier Preston Center submarket. The Property recently underwent a comprehensive renovation, including upgrades to its conference facilities, tenant lounge, café and fitness center. Sherry Lane Place is 93% leased as of closing to a diverse roster of institutional tenants, with a weighted-average lease term of approximately 6.6 years. Shorenstein plans to add wellness amenities and a bar lounge, enhance the lobby, and upgrade outdoor seating areas. Since June 2024, Shorenstein has acquired 13 office properties totaling approximately $2 billion. Combined, the office properties acquired as of June 2026 produced an average distribution yield of 8%. The post Shorenstein Adds 300K-SF Dallas Office Tower to DFW Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Shorenstein acquired Sherry Lane Place, 300K-SF Class AA tower in Dallas Preston Center, 93% leased
Shorenstein deployed $2B across 13 office properties since June 2024, averaging 8% distribution yield
Recent renovations and planned wellness/lounge upgrades signal flight-to-quality in DFW office market
stories.summary: Shorenstein Investment Advisers acquired the 300,000-square-foot, recently renovated Sherry Lane Place office tower in Dallas' Preston Center submarket, marking its fourth DFW acquisition in two years. The 20-story Class AA tower is 93% leased with a 6.6-year weighted-average lease term. Since June 2024, Shorenstein has acquired 13 office properties totaling approximately $2 billion, producing an average distribution yield of 8%, signaling institutional confidence in the office asset class recovery.
stories.impact: Office capital recycling into premium, leased assets in Dallas signals institutional belief in DFW's office stabilization, but does NOT directly affect multifamily supply or demand. However, sustained office occupancy and capital inflow into DFW reinforce the metro's employment durability and affluent tenant base, which supports pricing power and occupancy for Class A and luxury multifamily in submarkets proximate to Preston Center and downtown Dallas.

stories.title: GoDocs Sees Rise in Multifamily Lending Volume, Loan Size
stories.excerpt: Commercial loan document automation platform GoDocs said Tuesday it saw a 17.2% year-over-year increase in commercial loans for multifamily properties through its platform in the first half of 2026. Along with an increase in the number of loans, GoDocs also saw an 8.3% Y-O-Y increase in the size of multifamily loans, with the growth skewing at the larger end of loans making the mean increase 23.3%. Multifamily lending data on the GoDocs platform points in the same direction as the broader multifamily market. Newmark, for example, reported historically strong apartment demand alongside a 26% year-over-year increase in multifamily debt originations in H1 2026. After a first quarter that saw a 52.9% Y-O-Y increase, multifamily lending slowed slightly in Q2, with volume falling 3.3% below the year-ago period. “Still, that wasn’t significant enough to offset the strength earlier in the year, leaving H1 2026 volume 17.2% above H1 2025 overall,” GoDocs reported.”As H2 data emerges throughout the rest of 2026, we’ll be watching to determine whether the Q2 slowdown was temporary and how quickly growth resumes.” If you’re reading about the multifamily industry, you should be in the room with its leaders. Connect Apartments brings together the executives featured in Connect CRE’s coverage for an afternoon of high-level insights and unmatched networking on September 22 at The Biltmore in LA. The post GoDocs Sees Rise in Multifamily Lending Volume, Loan Size appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Multifamily lending volume up 17.2% Y-O-Y H1 2026; loan sizes up 8.3%, mean increase 23.3% skewing large
Newmark reported 26% Y-O-Y multifamily debt origination growth H1 2026; Q2 slowed 3.3% below year-ago
Q1 2026 saw 52.9% Y-O-Y surge; Q2 deceleration raises questions about capital flow sustainability through H2
stories.summary: GoDocs reported a 17.2% year-over-year increase in multifamily loan volume through its platform in H1 2026, with loan sizes growing 8.3% and skewing toward larger deals (mean increase 23.3%). Newmark corroborated this with a 26% Y-O-Y multifamily debt origination increase. However, Q2 2026 volume softened 3.3% below the year-ago period after a robust Q1 (up 52.9% Y-O-Y), raising questions about whether growth will sustain through H2.
stories.impact: Strong H1 2026 multifamily lending growth—particularly in larger loan sizes—signals capital availability and lender appetite for stabilized assets, supporting acquisition and refinance activity across markets. The Q2 slowdown warrants monitoring; if H2 decelerates further, construction financing for new development could tighten, especially for smaller or less-seasoned sponsors, which would compress starts in competitive markets and reduce near-term supply competition.

stories.title: Ian Schrager, Ed Scheetz Land $117M Refi for Public Hotel West Hollywood
stories.excerpt: Hoteliers Ian Schrager and Ed Scheetz have secured $116.5 million of bridge debt to refinance a Los Angeles hotel set to make its Hollywood debut. Driftwood Capital and Benefit Street Partners provided the loan for the Public Hotel West Hollywood, scheduled to open on the Sunset Strip in September at the site of the former Standard Hotel. Schrager and Scheetz redeveloped the property after acquiring it for $112.5 million in early 2023 two years after the Standard Hotel closed. Cushman & Wakefield negotiated the debt with a team led by Rob Rubano, JP LeVeque and Joe Lieske. “The quality of the asset and the strength of the sponsorship led to a strong financing execution that positions the property for long-term success,” Rubano, executive vice chair and head of equity, debt and structured finance at C&W, said in a statement. “We are seeing a significant resurgence across the Sunset Strip, and the timing could not be better for Public to capitalize on the momentum and anticipation building around this widely anticipated reopening.” The 137-key hotel at 8300 Sunset Boulevard has gone through a ground-up renovation program since Schrager and Scheetz purchased the site. Guest rooms and suites have been redesigned, and amenities such as a new rooftop deck and nightclub were added. Schraeger, Scheetz, Driftwood Capital and Benefit Street Partners did not immediately return requests for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Schrager & Scheetz secured $116.5M bridge refi for Public Hotel West Hollywood; September 2026 opening
Property acquired for $112.5M in early 2023; substantial redevelopment post-Standard Hotel closure
Driftwood Capital & Benefit Street Partners provided debt; C&W noted strong sponsorship and Sunset Strip resurgence
stories.summary: Ian Schrager and Ed Scheetz obtained $116.5 million in bridge debt from Driftwood Capital and Benefit Street Partners to refinance the Public Hotel West Hollywood, scheduled to open on the Sunset Strip in September 2026. The developers acquired the site (former Standard Hotel) for $112.5 million in early 2023 and completed a full redevelopment. Cushman & Wakefield negotiated the transaction and highlighted strong sponsorship strength and a significant Sunset Strip resurgence.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. However, successful hotel refinancing and capital deployment on Sunset Strip signals broader West Hollywood / central LA tourism and hospitality recovery, which can boost adjacent residential demand and rent growth from service workers and hospitality-adjacent employees; monitor if this redevelopment catalyst spurs nearby multifamily acquisitions or new starts in Hollywood submarket.

stories.title: Passco Offloads Buckhead Rental Asset for $87.5M
stories.excerpt: ORIX Corporation USA purchased The Kendrick, a 423-unit multifamily property, for $87.5 million. Built in 1998, the garden-style multifamily community is located in Atlanta’s Buckhead neighborhood, near major employment, retail and entertainment centers. The business plan includes capital improvements to modernize units and common areas. It was part of a three multifamily portfolio totaling 1,029 units in Texas and Georgia. The Atlanta Business Chronicle reports that Passco Companies was the seller. The company purchased the community in late 2019 for about $106 million. The community is located along Canterbury Road near the interchange of Interstate 85 and State Route 400, about 2.5 miles south of Buckhead’s commercial corridor. Apartment homes offer one-, two- and three-bedroom floor plans and measure up to 2,300 square feet. Amenities include a pool area, an aqua lounge, tennis courts, a three-story clubhouse with a game room and a club-style fitness center. The post Passco Offloads Buckhead Rental Asset for $87.5M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: ORIX acquired 423-unit Kendrick garden-style apt in Atlanta Buckhead for $87.5M; seller Passco paid $106M in late 2019
Property near I-85/SR-400 interchange, 2.5 miles south of Buckhead commercial core; plans capital improvements
Sale reflects value compression; built 1998, suggesting aging asset in premium submarket facing cap rate pressure
stories.summary: ORIX Corporation USA purchased The Kendrick, a 423-unit garden-style multifamily community in Atlanta's Buckhead for $87.5 million. Passco Companies sold the asset after acquiring it in late 2019 for approximately $106 million, taking a realized loss of roughly $18.5 million. Located near the I-85/SR-400 interchange, 2.5 miles south of Buckhead's commercial core, ORIX plans capital improvements to modernize units and common areas.
stories.impact: Passco's loss-on-sale signals value compression in Buckhead's secondary locations despite strong Atlanta demand; 1998-vintage garden-style product lacking modern amenities underperforms versus newer Class A stock. For developers, this indicates limited pricing power for aging mid-market product in Buckhead and underscores competitive pressure from newly delivered institutional-quality supply; New development or substantial value-add conversions in Buckhead should target primary corridors and modern product mix to justify premiums.

stories.title: Trammell Crow-Led Team Delivers 686K-SF Atlanta-Area Warehouse Facility
stories.excerpt: Trammell Crow Company and its joint venture partner, a consortium led by CBRE Japan, have delivered Buford Creek Business Center, a three-building, 686,400-square-foot speculative industrial park in Buford, Georgia, approximately 30 miles northeast of Atlanta. CBRE’s Todd Barton, Mark Hawks, Joanna Blaesing, and Matt Higgins are marketing the buildings for sale or lease on behalf of ownership.Buford Creek Business Center is located at the northeast corner of Lanier Islands Parkway and Big Creek Road in Buford, three miles from Interstate 985. Building 100 is a 40-foot clear, 349,440-square-foot cross-dock warehouse with 64 trailer parking spots. Buildings 200 and 300 are identical in size at 168,400 square feet. They both have 36-foot clear heights and are rear-load buildings with 40 and 24 trailer parking spots, respectively.Buford Creek Business Center was designed by Atlas Collaborative and built by The Conlan Company. bullets: Trammell Crow joint venture delivered 686.4K-SF Buford Creek Business Center, three-building industrial park, Buford GA
Project includes 349.4K-SF cross-dock (Building 100) plus two 168.4K-SF rear-load warehouses (Buildings 200, 300)

stories.summary: Trammell Crow Company and a CBRE Japan-led consortium delivered Buford Creek Business Center, a three-building, 686,400-square-foot speculative industrial park in Buford, Georgia, approximately 30 miles northeast of Atlanta. Building 100 is a 349,440-square-foot, 40-foot clear cross-dock facility; Buildings 200 and 300 are 168,400-square-foot rear-load facilities with 36-foot clear heights. The site is located three miles from Interstate 985 at the northeast corner of Lanier Islands Parkway and Big Creek Road.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. However, speculative industrial delivery in Buford signals robust logistics and e-commerce demand in Northeast Atlanta exurbs, which drives job creation and wage growth for warehouse and distribution workers. This employment base supports multifamily demand in lower-cost suburban rings (Buford, Suwanee, Cumming corridors) and can justify new renter-focused development targeting service-sector and warehouse workers seeking affordability relative to central Atlanta; monitor absorption and tenant quality to assess labor stability and wage sustainability.

stories.title: After Foreclosure Saga, Charles Cohen Plans Office Complex in Florida’s Dania Beach
stories.excerpt: Charles Cohen is rising from the ashes of foreclosure with plans to build a speculative office complex in Dania Beach, Fla., near Fort Lauderdale’s main airport. The billionaire developer’s firm, Cohen Brothers Realty Corporation of Florida, is launching the Office Center of the Americas (OCOTA), a two-building development with 400,000 square feet of office space, Commercial Observer has learned. The Nichols Brosch Wurst Wolfe & Associates-designed development will be delivered in two phases and is expected to cost about $350 million. The two buildings will each rise 10 stories and have a four-story parking garage attached at 1805 and 1815 Griffin Road facing Interstate 95, just south of Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport. Cooper Horowitz is handling construction financing for the project. A representative for Cohen declined to comment on the construction timeline. OCOTA will be erected next to the Design Center of the Americas (DCOTA), a mixed-use complex that Cohen lost two years ago in foreclosure to his former lender Fortress Investment Group. Just last month, the New York-based lender, now owner, nabbed $45 million to refinance the 780,000-square-foot office and design showroom complex. The foreclosure between Fortress Investment Group and Cohen turned contentious when the lender went after the New York billionaire’s personal assets, including a chateau and vineyard estate in the south of France, a 220-foot megayacht, and a collection of Ferrari sports cars. In June, Cohen announced that he had paid off the full judgment. Cohen has revived plans for another 400,000-square-foot office project, this time in Downtown West Palm Beach. In July, the developer filed for permits after resolving a foreclosure lawsuit over a $10 million loan tied to the 2.4-acre site, The Real Deal reported. bullets: Charles Cohen planning 400K-SF Office Center of Americas (OCOTA) in Dania Beach near Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood Airport

Speculative office complex follows Cohen's foreclosure challenges; project positioning for South Florida's logistics/aerospace employment proximity
stories.summary: Charles Cohen's Cohen Brothers Realty Corporation of Florida is launching the Office Center of the Americas (OCOTA), a two-building, 400,000-square-foot speculative office development in Dania Beach near Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport. The NICBR-designed project will feature two 10-story office towers with attached four-story parking and is expected to cost approximately $350 million, delivered in two phases. Cooper Horowitz is arranging construction financing.
stories.impact: Speculative office development near FLL airport reflects bet on South Florida aviation, logistics, and aerospace employment clusters, but represents capital that could alternatively flow to multifamily. Large-scale office permitting and construction near FLL may compete for labor and materials with residential projects in greater Fort Lauderdale; however, office job creation at/near airport does support downstream multifamily demand. Monitor construction progress and pre-leasing traction; weak pre-leasing could signal South Florida office overbuilding and capital misallocation away from multifamily.

stories.title: A COGE Member On How New York City Can Boost Affordable Housing
stories.excerpt: Two extremely troubling recent headlines underscored the mounting challenges in addressing New York City’s affordable housing crisis: Rents hit a record high while the number of vacancies in denser boroughs plummeted. These headlines underscore how far we have to go to ensure every New Yorker has a stable, quality home that doesn’t break the bank. Data show that the median average monthly rent on new leases in Manhattan surged to a record high of $5,000 in July — up 6.4 percent from 2025 — while the number of available units plunged by more than 69 percent. In Brooklyn, the median rent hit a record $4,500 a month, with available units dropping by 27 percent. Carlina Rivera. Photo: Courtesy NYSASAF. In addition, in August, the Mamdani administration announced that just 12,491 affordable homes were preserved or created in the first six months of 2026 — the lowest half-year total since 2022. We all know that New York City is one of the most expensive places in the nation, if not the world, to build affordable housing. This is due to a wide array of factors, from rising insurance costs to the scarcity of land and a byzantine permitting and regulatory system. Against this backdrop and recognizing that there are some matters outside its control, it’s critical that the government do everything in its power to make it easier, faster and more cost-efficient to build and preserve affordable units in all five boroughs. The Mamdani administration has taken steps in the right direction with the proposed Streamlining Procedures to Expedite Equitable Development (SPEED) reforms and the Block-by-Block housing plan. Now voters can help build on this progress by approving the ballot proposals advanced by the mayor’s Commission on Government Efficiency (COGE) in the November election. I had the privilege of serving on COGE. Together with my fellow commission members, we spent months hearing from a range of residents, business owners, advocates and elected officials from every borough
bullets: Manhattan median rent hit record $5,000/month in July 2026, up 6.4% Y-O-Y; vacancy plunged 69%
Brooklyn median rent reached $4,500/month (record); units available dropped 27%; supply shortage extreme
NYC affordable housing production fell to 12,491 units H1 2026, lowest half-year since 2022; crisis deepening
stories.summary: New York City's rental crisis intensified in mid-2026: Manhattan median rent surged to a record $5,000 per month (up 6.4% Y-O-Y) while available units plunged more than 69%. Brooklyn saw median rent hit $4,500 (also record) with a 27% drop in available units. The Mamdani administration reported only 12,491 affordable homes preserved or created in H1 2026, the lowest half-year total since 2022, highlighting the city's inability to match demand with supply.
stories.impact: Critical multifamily signal: NYC is experiencing severe supply shortage amid record rents, indicating undersupply relative to demand. For developers, this reveals an entitlement and capital opportunity in NYC (Manhattan, Brooklyn, outer boroughs) for both market-rate and affordable product, though permitting delays, construction costs, and financing hurdles remain barriers. The absence of affordable production and the 69% vacancy collapse in Manhattan suggest pent-up demand for quality rental housing at all price points; developers with entitlements and capital should accelerate permitting and starts in NYC before further policy tightening or recession pressures financing.

stories.title: Mann Group Buys Luxury Apartments at 130 Hope Street in Williamsburg
stories.excerpt: Clipper Equity’s hopes have been realized in the sale of a luxury rental building at 130 Hope Street in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, Commercial Observer has learned. Clipper sold the 150-unit building — which it completed in 2023 and dubbed Casa Hope — to New York City-based investor and developer the Mann Group for $122.5 million, according to broker Rosewood Realty Group. One-bedroom units in the new development just one block east of the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway start at $4,700 per month. “The sale of 130 Hope Street reflects the strong demand we’re seeing for new construction properties across the boroughs. With a 35-year, 421-a tax abatement in place, buyers benefit from decades of low property taxes paired with a mainly free-market building,” Rosewood’s Alex Fuchs said in a statement. “Williamsburg continues to be one of the most desirable neighborhoods in Brooklyn, and this marks the second new construction sale we’ve closed in the neighborhood this quarter,” Fuchs added. Fuchs represented the seller and arranged the buyer alongside Aaron Jungreis and Ben Khakshoor of Rosewood. Spokespeople for Clipper and the Mann Group did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The other Williamsburg deal mentioned by Fuchs was likely the sale of 227 Grand Street by Hutton Capital to Michael Shah’s DelShah Capital back in early July as part of a larger acquisition sweep of mixed-use residential properties in Williamsburg amounting to $127.8 million. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Mann Group acquired 150-unit Casa Hope at 130 Hope Street Williamsburg from Clipper Equity for $122.5M
Property completed 2023; one-bedroom units starting at $4,700/month; 35-year 421-a tax abatement in place
Rosewood noted strong new construction demand across NYC boroughs; second new construction sale in Williamsburg this quarter
stories.summary: Clipper Equity sold the 150-unit luxury rental building Casa Hope at 130 Hope Street in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, to Mann Group for $122.5 million. Completed in 2023, the building offers one-bedroom units starting at $4,700 per month and benefits from a 35-year 421-a tax abatement. Broker Rosewood Realty Group noted this represents strong buyer demand for new construction across the boroughs, marking the second such sale in Williamsburg this quarter.
stories.impact: Williamsburg rental market showing robust institutional buyer appetite for newer Class A product with long-term tax benefits, validating new construction economics in high-cost Brooklyn submarkets. Sale at $122.5M for 150 units (~$817K/unit) affirms pricing power for modern product and 421-a abatement value; however, rising rents ($4,700 one-bed) signal tightening affordability and may prompt policy-driven rent regulation or inclusionary zoning expansion. Developers should accelerate Williamsburg and similar hot Brooklyn neighborhoods before further rent caps or mandatory affordability requirements erode project returns.

stories.title: New York-Based Henry AI Has a New End-to-End Deal-Making Portal
stories.excerpt: In a world increasingly dominated by artificial intelligence, some platforms are busy gaining steam despite catering to one of the pickiest market segments. In June, Henry AI — an AI platform founded by Sammy Greenwall and Adam Pratt that automates back-office work for commercial real estate brokerages — sealed a $16.5 million Series A funding round led by FirstMark Capital. The Series A came only two years after the company’s inception, and happily coincided with Henry’s next iteration. “We needed to be a platform and not just a wedge product,” Greenwall said. “The vast majority of customers in the market know us as a deck-making tool and not as a deal-generation, end-to-end platform. So Adam and his team went through a crazy sprint over the space of 45 to 60 days to effectively build an entirely new platform from scratch.” That new platform, Henry Deal, represented a leveling up of Henry AI and was the catalyst for the Series A launch. Essentially, while Henry AI began with offering memorandums, underwriting and pitch decks, Henry Deal covers every stage from initial underwriting all the way through packaging and closing. The platform provides full underwriting capabilities and a comps database. It can also build market reports, buyer lists, lender lists and even pitch a deal for you. Henry Deal was built in only 35 days or so, but Greenwall and Pratt didn’t want the market to know about it until it was piloted and deeply embedded with multiple enterprise organizations on the brokerage side. “We’ve spent a very long period of time staying very focused on one product, refining it and improving it over time,” Pratt said. “I think one advantage we had is that we learned so much about our users’ workflows by onboarding decks and fixing things there that a lot of the same things are true. bullets: Henry AI raised $16.5M Series A led by FirstMark Capital; expanded from deck-making tool to end-to-end deal platform
Henry Deal covers entire transaction workflow from underwriting through deal closing; launched June 2026
Platform automates back-office work for CRE brokerages; broadened scope signals CRE tech market maturation and consolidation pressure
stories.summary: Henry AI, an AI platform automating back-office work for commercial real estate brokerages, secured $16.5 million in Series A funding led by FirstMark Capital. The company launched Henry Deal, an end-to-end deal-making portal covering initial underwriting through closing, expanding beyond its original offering memorandum and pitch-deck functionality. Co-founders Sammy Greenwall and Adam Pratt emphasized the shift from a specialized tool to a comprehensive platform.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily supply or demand. However, Henry AI's platform expansion and Series A funding underscore growing efficiency gains and AI-driven automation in CRE deal origination and execution, which may accelerate transaction velocity and lower deal costs for multifamily sponsors. Faster, cheaper deal automation could flatten transaction margins for brokers and underwriting firms, incentivizing consolidation or specialization; indirectly, lower deal friction may accelerate capital deployment into multifamily acquisitions and refinances across markets.

stories.title: Eastwind Building 264-Unit Melbourne Apartment Community
stories.excerpt: Eastwind Development began construction of The Aston at Longleaf, a 264-unit luxury apartment community on Preserve Drive in Melbourne, Florida. The beginning of construction immediately follows Eastwind’s closing on the acquisition of the 17-acre project site and a $45.5 million construction loan provided by TD. Situated in Florida’s Space Coast region, The Aston at Longleaf is targeting delivery of the first units in late 2027, with full project completion expected by mid-2028. The development team includes FaverGray as general contractor, FK Architecture as project architect, and Kimley-Horn as project engineer. Residents will enjoy access to amenities that include an expansive 10,000-square-foot clubhouse featuring a vibrant community lounge and game room with multiple social areas; a fitness center with an adjoining spin room; a spacious coworking lounge; and a multi-sport gaming simulator room. Outdoors, a resort-style swimming pool with private cabanas, an outdoor kitchen, a fire pit, a yoga lawn and a games lawn. bullets: Eastwind Development began construction of 264-unit Aston at Longleaf in Melbourne, Florida Space Coast region

stories.summary: Eastwind Development commenced construction on The Aston at Longleaf, a 264-unit luxury apartment community in Melbourne, Florida, on the Space Coast. The developer closed on the 17-acre site acquisition and a $45.5 million construction loan from TD Bank. First units are targeted for late 2027, with full project completion by mid-2028. The community features a 10,000-square-foot clubhouse, resort-style pool with cabanas, coworking lounge, and multi-sport gaming simulator.
stories.impact: Melbourne/Space Coast multifamily growth signals investor confidence in Florida's Space Coast region as a secondary demand driver (aerospace, defense, tech, retiree migration). 264-unit new construction in a 30+ mile radius from major employment (Kennedy Space Center, contractors, defense aerospace) supports job and wage growth. Completion in late 2027–mid-2028 adds supply; monitor Space Coast rent growth and absorption trends to assess whether new supply absorbs or compresses rents. This delivery timeline positions Eastwind ahead of potential recession; if demand softens, Space Coast rents and occupancy could face pressure from concurrent deliveries.
